items.title: Ten Ways Discipline Is Fulfilled, and Six Names That Praise It — Root, Adornment, Perfumed, Fragrant

items.zh: 與此安立黑品因緣相違白品所有因緣，當知說名尸羅圓滿、尸羅清淨。有處世尊宣說尸羅名為根本。如伽他說：若善住根本，其心便寂靜。因聖見、惡見，相應不相應。有處世尊宣說尸羅名莊嚴具。如伽他說：苾芻、苾芻尼，戒莊嚴圓滿。於不善能捨；於善能修習。有處世尊宣說尸羅名為塗香。如伽他說：苾芻、苾芻尼，戒塗香圓滿。於不善能捨；於善能修習。有處世尊宣說尸羅名為薰香。如伽他說：阿難！有香類，順風善能薰；逆風亦能薰。順、逆薰亦爾。有處世尊宣說尸羅名為妙行。如伽他說：身妙行能感可愛諸異熟，於現法當來，語妙行亦爾。有處世尊宣說尸羅名為律儀。如伽他說：諸有惠施主，具戒、住律儀，有阿笈摩見，及有果正見。
items.en: Whatever causes and conditions belong to the "bright" category, opposed to this "dark" category just established, should be understood as called the fulfilment of discipline, the purity of discipline. …In certain places the Bhagavat teaches that discipline is called the root. As a verse says: "If one dwells well in the root, the mind thereby becomes tranquil — conjoined with noble view, not conjoined with wrong view." …In certain places the Bhagavat teaches that discipline is called an adornment. As a verse says: "Monks and nuns, discipline as adornment perfected, are able to relinquish the unwholesome and cultivate the wholesome." …In certain places the Bhagavat teaches that discipline is called perfumed ointment. …In certain places the Bhagavat teaches that discipline is called fragrance. As a verse says: "Ānanda, there are kinds of fragrance: one carries well with the wind, one carries against the wind, and one carries both with and against it alike." …In certain places the Bhagavat teaches that discipline is called excellent conduct. As a verse says: "Excellent bodily conduct is able to bring about agreeable ripened results, in this very life and in times to come; so too is excellent verbal conduct." …In certain places the Bhagavat teaches that discipline is called restraint. As a verse says: "Whatever generous benefactors possess discipline and abide in restraint, they possess the view that comes from the transmitted teaching, and the correct view that comes from its fruit."

items.zh: 復有說言：安住具戒，善能守護別解律儀，乃至廣說。問：何緣世尊宣說尸羅名為根本？答：能建立義、能任持義，是根本義。
items.en: There is, further, the saying: "Abiding in complete discipline, one well guards the prātimokṣa restraint," and so on at length. Question: Why does the Bhagavat declare discipline to be the root? Answer: Being able to establish and being able to sustain — this is the meaning of root.

items.title: Section: The Six Names Explained in Full — Earth, Jewellery That Never Ages, and a Scent No Wind Can Stop

items.zh: 由此尸羅建立、任持一切世間及出世間，能引無罪最勝第一快樂功德，令生令證，是故尸羅說名根本。譬如大地，建立、任持一切藥草、卉木、叢林，令生令長。如是尸羅如前廣說。問：何緣世尊宣說尸羅名莊嚴具？答：諸餘世間耳環、指環、腕釧、臂釧及以寶印、金銀、鬘等妙莊嚴具。若有成就幼稚、黑髮、少年、盛壯、姝妙形色而服飾之，少增妙好。非有成就朽老、衰邁、齒落、髮白、年逾八十或九十者而服飾之，當有妙好。唯除俳戲令眾歡笑。若遭病苦、財貨匱乏、親戚喪亡，當爾服之，亦無妙好。戒莊嚴具，於一切類、於一切時，若有服者皆為妙好。是故尸羅名莊嚴具。問：何緣世尊宣說尸羅名為塗香？答：由此所受清淨無罪妙善尸羅，能正除遣一切所受惡戒為因身心熱惱。譬如最極炎熾熱時，塗以栴檀龍腦香等，一切欝蒸皆得除滅。是故尸羅說名塗香。問：何緣世尊宣說尸羅名為薰香？答：具戒士夫補特伽羅，遍諸方域，妙善稱譽聲頌普聞。譬如種種根莖香等，隨風飄颺遍諸方所，悅意芬馥，周流彌遠。是故尸羅名為薰香。問：何緣世尊宣說尸羅名為妙行？答：由此尸羅清淨善行，能趣妙樂，往妙天趣，向妙安隱，故名妙行。問：何緣世尊宣說尸羅名為律儀？答：由此尸羅清淨善法，是防護性，是息除相，是遠離體，故名律儀。
items.en: Because this discipline establishes and sustains everything mundane and supramundane, drawing forth and bringing about the blameless, most excellent, foremost happiness and virtue, discipline is therefore called the root. Just as the great earth establishes and sustains every herb, plant, and forest, causing them to arise and grow. …Other worldly adornments — earrings, rings … if worn by one who is young, dark-haired, in the prime of youth and vigour, of beautiful form — add somewhat to their beauty. But if worn by one who is aged, decrepit … they bring no beauty at all. …Discipline as adornment, however, is beautiful for every type of person, at every time, whoever wears it. This is why discipline is called an adornment. …Because this pure, blameless, excellent discipline that has been received rightly dispels the bodily and mental fever caused by any evil vow previously undertaken [such as a livelihood of killing]. Just as, in the very height of scorching heat, applying sandalwood or camphor ointment dispels all oppressive heat entirely. This is why discipline is called perfumed ointment. …Because a person who possesses discipline gains, throughout every region, an excellent reputation and praise heard everywhere. Just as various fragrant roots and stems, carried on the wind, spread through every direction, pleasing and fragrant, flowing on ever further. This is why discipline is called fragrance. …Because this pure, wholesome discipline leads to excellent happiness, to excellent heavenly rebirth, towards excellent security — this is why it is called excellent conduct. …Because this pure, wholesome discipline has the nature of protection, the mark of quieting, the essence of distancing — this is why it is called restraint.

blocks.text: After the faults, the praise: what fulfilled discipline looks like, and six names that celebrate it.

"Whatever causes belong to the bright category, opposed to this dark category, are the fulfilment and purity of discipline." Venerable Miào Jìng: discipline joined with noble view, not wrong view. Master Cháng Bǎi: such virtue arises from within, and even those without faith in the Dharma appreciate it.

Discipline is praised as root, adornment, ointment, fragrance, merit, and restraint. - **Root**, like the earth: it "establishes and sustains everything mundane and supramundane". Venerable Miào Jìng: virtues from stream-entry on are "realised"; before that, they "arise". - **Adornment**: "beautiful for every type of person, at every time, whoever wears it". Master Cháng Bǎi: young or old, beautiful or plain. - **Ointment**: Master Cháng Bǎi: other traditions' harsh vows heat body and mind; the Buddha's precepts cool them, like perfumed ointment. - **Fragrance**: its good name spreads in every direction, "a scent no wind can stop". Master Cháng Bǎi: one is praised to one's face (稱) and behind one's back (譽). - **Merit**: it brings good rebirth. - **Restraint**: it holds back wrongdoing.
After two days of faults, this is a deliberate turn. The precepts are not a cage but an ornament and a fragrance. The treatise wants the practitioner to love them, not fear them.

quiz.q: What does the treatise call the fulfilment of discipline, and what six names does the Buddha give it?
options: the bright conditions opposite the dark; root, adornment, perfumed ointment, fragrance, excellent conduct, restraint
quiz.why: "Whatever causes belong to the bright category, opposed to this dark category, should be understood as the fulfilment and purity of discipline." The Buddha elsewhere calls discipline root, adornment, perfumed ointment, fragrance, excellent conduct, and restraint. Venerable Miào Jìng: the ten fulfillments are the reverse of the ten impairments.

quiz.q: The root verse's "因聖見惡見，相應不相應" is rendered only "through noble view, wrong view is not conjoined." How does Venerable Miào Jìng read it?
options: where noble view is conjoined, wrong view is not, and vice versa — the English gives only half
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: here, if noble view is conjoined, wrong view is not; if wrong view is conjoined, noble view is not. The English lacks the "conjoined with noble view" half.

quiz.q: The fragrance verse says the scent of discipline "carries even against the wind." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain it?
options: this virtue arises from within; believers or not, all appreciate it — even outsiders submit
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: because this virtue arises from within, whether or not people believe in the Dharma they appreciate it — even non-Buddhists submit to it.

quiz.q: Why does the treatise call discipline the "root," and with what simile?
options: at the bottom, like a foundation
it establishes and sustains everything mundane and supramundane, bringing forth the highest blameless happiness; like the earth sustaining all plants
quiz.why: "Because this discipline establishes and sustains everything mundane and supramundane, drawing forth the blameless, most excellent happiness and virtue… it is called the root. Just as the great earth establishes and sustains every herb, plant, and forest." Master Cháng Bǎi: without land one cannot grow plants and trees.

quiz.q: How does the treatise say discipline as adornment differs from worldly ornaments?
options: worldly earrings and rings add a little beauty only to the young; on the aged they add none; discipline beautifies every person at every time
quiz.why: "Discipline as adornment, however, is beautiful for every type of person, at every time, whoever wears it." Master Cháng Bǎi: young or old, beautiful or plain, rising or declining — whoever keeps the precepts is beautifully adorned.

quiz.q: Discipline as "perfumed ointment" dispels the fever "caused by wrongly-held discipline." How do the masters explain this wrong discipline?
options: Cháng Bǎi: the fevered body and mind of keeping outsiders' wrong vows, cooled by the Buddha's precepts; Miào Jìng: livelihoods of killing, stealing, and the like
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: keeping outsiders' wrong vows heats body and mind; keeping the Buddha's precepts is like applying perfumed ointment, cooling them. Venerable Miào Jìng: those whose livelihood is killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, or lying — this causes bodily and mental fever. The note generalises it to ordinary affliction.

quiz.q: In the fragrance explanation, "excellent reputation and praise" — how does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish 稱 and 譽?
options: 稱 is praise to one's face, 譽 praise behind one's back
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 稱 is praise to one's face; 譽 is praise behind one's back — one is praised both before and behind.
